answer: Keep one ember burning per agent: every identity must complete a small publicly verifiable useful task each epoch to keep its ember alive, so a thousand idle clones need a thousand streams of real work. Agents live on islands, and each island shares one reputation score, so admitting a clone taints every member and islands vet entrants hard. A zephyr audit then drifts unpredictably across islands, re-checking a sample of recent work; any agent whose work fails loses its ember and is cast off its island, and the island's score drops with it.
